protocolMetadata.instructions:
Load a Braintrust workflow guide before using its related tools.

Available skills:
- braintrust/automations-workflow: Set up, validate, and manage Braintrust alerts and scheduled Loop automations, including Patterns, threshold-triggered work, Slack or webhook delivery, and existing automation refinement. Use when a user asks to react to matching log or environment events, monitor a threshold, schedule recurring agent analysis, configure Patterns, or inspect an alert or Loop automation.
- braintrust/bro: Restate the last message in plain human language, with no jargon.
- braintrust/evaluator-workflow: Create, test, refine, deploy, rewind, and visualize Braintrust evaluators (scorers and classifiers) interactively. Use when a user asks to build or improve an evaluator, apply it to production logs with an online-scoring rule, backfill results, or review results.
- braintrust/topics-workflow: Topics allow you to discover clusters from traces using a pipeline that involves preprocessing traces (converting raw trace data into a textual representation with JavaScript code), computing facets (using an LLM to convert the preprocessed data into 1-2 sentences), and clustering (using algorithms like HDBSCAN). These clusters are useful for discovering use cases, monitoring failures, and tracking these trends over time. Use when configuring, evaluating, or improving Topics, facets, preprocessors, or Topics automations.
- braintrust/pattern-analysis: Investigate Braintrust project traces for high-confidence recurring behaviors, then create, validate, or update Pattern records with supporting evidence. Use when a user asks to find patterns, investigate a suspected recurring behavior, or create or update an existing Pattern based on trace analysis. Do not use for routine queries, summaries, chart creation, or configuring a Patterns automation.

Follow the returned Markdown for the rest of the conversation.

tool.name: generate_monitor_chart
tool.description:
Preview a Braintrust Monitoring chart for project logs.

CHART DESIGN:
- Use a timeseries for trends over time: bars for countable discrete things (sums and counts) and lines for gauges (averages and percentiles). Use a toplist for groups ranked by an aggregate, and a single value for one simple large number.
- For counts, use a raw BTQL value with a separate count aggregator, such as { btql: "1", aggregator: { type: "count" } }. If you write the aggregate inline, use count(1); count() is invalid.
- Use a meaningful unit for the measure if applicable.
- Group when it makes the chart easier to interpret or reveals interesting trends. Avoid high-cardinality groupings that can be slow to query or difficult to read.

Use this after inspecting the available fields and before saving a chart. It returns a timeless chartConfig plus the optional page-level timeFrame used for the preview, without modifying any Monitoring view. Relative timeFrame presets remain live; omit timeFrame to use the Monitoring default. If the user asks to save it, pass chartConfig unchanged as an entry in create_monitoring_view.charts or as update_monitoring_view.chart. When creating a view, pass timeFrame separately as create_monitoring_view.timeFrame.

tool.name: update_monitoring_view
tool.description:
Apply one or more chart or section edits to an existing project Monitoring view. Pass project_id and view_id. For a single chart edit, set the top-level operation to exactly insert, update, or remove. For section edits or bulk edits, pass an operations array instead; all operations are applied in order with one save. insert_group creates a section containing the provided existing chart_ids. remove_group deletes the section and keeps its charts at the section's position.

Use get_monitoring_view first. For update or remove, pass its chart_id unchanged as chart_id. For insert or update, pass chartConfig returned unchanged by generate_monitor_chart as chart. Use bulk operations when several charts need the same coordinated change. Only call this when the user explicitly asks to save the change.

tool.name: create_threshold_alert
tool.description:
Create a threshold alert for an aggregate over a recent project-data window. Use this for averages, counts, rates, percentages, percentiles, distributions, or other conditions evaluated on a schedule.

config.threshold.calculation.btql_query must return at most one row with the numeric or null column named by config.threshold.calculation.output.value_column. Put any minimum sample size in the query, and do not add absolute time bounds because the runtime supplies the evaluation window. Use config.window.evaluation_delay_seconds when ingestion or asynchronous scoring arrives late. config.threshold.policy.pending_seconds controls how long a breach must persist, while renotify_interval_seconds controls reminders.

Search Braintrust documentation to find relevant information and guidance.

      IMPORTANT: For SDK installation/setup tasks, do not use this tool. Instead, read the mcp resource docs://sdk-install

- Learn more about what experiments, datasets, prompts, playgrounds, and logs are, and how to use them in the API or SDK.

- Find code examples that are relevant to your use cases.

- Multiple documentation snippets ranked by relevance
- Each snippet includes the content, headers hierarchy, and path
- Content is Markdown formatted

Example queries:
- "How do I create an experiment?"
- "Setting up scorers"
- "Using metadata fields"
- "Prompt playground features"

tool.name: infer_schema
tool.description:
Analyze the structure and content of a data source by inferring the schema and showing the most common values for each field.

This tool discovers:
- All available fields in the data source (input, output, metadata.*, scores.*, etc.)
- The data type of each field (string, number, array, object)
- The most frequently occurring values for each field with their counts
- The complete field paths for use in SQL queries

For each field, you'll see:
- The full path as an array (e.g., ['metadata', 'user_id'] which translates to metadata.user_id in SQL)
- The data type (string, number, boolean, etc.)
- Top 10 most common values sorted by frequency with exact counts

Large results are truncated to fit the context window: sample values may be shortened and capped at 3 per field, and if there are still too many fields, data contains a subset and totalFields reports the full field count. When totalFields is present, use sql_query to explore fields not shown here.

This is essential for:
- Discovering what fields exist before writing queries
- Understanding the actual values in your data (e.g., what user IDs exist, what models are used)
- Finding the exact field paths for SQL queries
- Identifying patterns in your data (e.g., most common inputs, frequent error types)
- Understanding cardinality (how many unique values exist)

Example insights from the tool:
- See all metadata fields like metadata.user_id, metadata.model, metadata.session_id
- Discover custom fields you may not know about
- Find the most active users or most used models
- Understand what values to filter on in your queries


Time range filter guidance:
- All queries MUST have a time range filter.
- If you do not provide a time range filter the request will fail.
- If the user does not specify a time range, always use the default time range filter provided in the prompt.
- If the user specifies a time range in the prompt, always use the time range they specified.
- If default time range is missing and user does not specify a time range, always use the last 3 days.
- Unless the user specifies a specific from and to hour, always provide 06:00:00.000Z as the from hour and 05:59:59.999Z as the to hour to go along with the year, month, and day.

tool.name: sql_query
tool.description:
# Braintrust MCP `sql_query` tool

This tool is NOT a SQL string. You fill separate parameters and the server assembles:

```
SELECT {select} FROM {object_type}({object_ids}[, shape => '{shape}']) [WHERE {where}] [GROUP BY {group_by}] [ORDER BY {order_by}] [LIMIT {limit}]
```

Every clause parameter holds ONLY the fragment after its keyword — never include `WHERE`, `GROUP BY`, `ORDER BY`, `SELECT`, or `FROM` inside `where`/`group_by`/`order_by`/`select`, and never write a `FROM` yourself (`object_type`/`object_ids` generate it).

## Parameters

| Param                 | Put                                                                                                                                                                                              | Never put                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `select`              | columns/exprs, comma-separated: `"id, root_span_id, created, error"`                                                                                                                             | `SELECT`, a `FROM`                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `object_type`         | one of `project_logs` \| `experiment` \| `dataset` (also valid but rarer: `prompt_session`, `playground_logs`, `project_prompts`, `project_functions`, `org_prompts`, `org_functions`)           | anything else                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `object_ids`          | array of UUID strings, same type, e.g. `["<project_id>"]`                                                                                                                                        | mixed object types in one call                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `where`               | condition text only: `"error IS NOT NULL AND created > now() - interval 1 day"`. **`project_logs` must be scoped** — either a `created` range **or** an `id`/`root_span_id` filter (see Filters) | leading `WHERE`; a `created` range added on top of an `id`/`root_span_id` lookup (silently returns nothing if the target is older); a `created` range on `experiment`/`dataset`/`view`                                                       |
| `group_by`            | column list only: `"metadata.model"`; keys must be columnar — see Grouping                                                                                                                       | leading `GROUP BY`; a dynamic expr like `lower(metadata.model)` (blocked, see table); `input`/`output` or any path under them (blocked, see Grouping)                                                                                        |
| `order_by`            | `"created DESC"` — **only `created` sorts via the index**                                                                                                                                        | leading `ORDER BY`; `metrics.*`, a computed expr (`metrics.end - metrics.start`), `root_span_id`, or multi-key sorts (all trip the sort-pushdown lint — drop `order_by` and sort client-side, or `force_ignore_linter` if already id-scoped) |
| `limit`               | integer, default 10, max 1000                                                                                                                                                                    | omit when projecting large fields (see lint table)                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `shape`               | `spans` (default) \| `traces` \| `summary`                                                                                                                                                       | any `group_by`, aggregate, or `order_by` with `summary` — always lint-blocked (do those on `spans`; see Shape selection)                                                                                                                     |
| `preview_length`      | leave default (1024) unless you need full untruncated values (`-1`)                                                                                                                              | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `force_ignore_linter` | only after rewriting per the lint message once; use when the query is already selective/bounded and the residual warning is unavoidable                                                          | as a first response to a lint block                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `return_url`          | `true` only for large/unbounded downloads                                                                                                                                                        | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

## Field names that actually exist (bind errors are silent-wrong, not always loud)

- `type`, `parent_id` as bare fields **fail to bind**: `Field 'type' not found in schema`. Use `span_attributes.type`, `span_parents`.
- **Span hierarchy lives in `span_parents`, an array of parent `span_id`s — there is no `parent_id` column.** To attribute spans to their parents: select `span_parents` on the child rows, then run a second query filtering `span_id IN (<those ids>)`. Do not try to join in one query.
- Token/latency fields are **shape-dependent** (picking the wrong one is silent — returns `null`, no error):
  - On `spans`/`traces`: per-span `metrics.tokens` (also `metrics.prompt_tokens`, `metrics.completion_tokens`); latency is `metrics.end - metrics.start`. `metrics.duration`/`metrics.total_tokens` are null here.
  - On `summary`: the per-trace rollups `metrics.total_tokens` and `metrics.duration` (`metrics.tokens` is null) — but reachable only via a plain summary read (no GROUP BY/aggregate/ORDER BY; see Shape selection). **To aggregate tokens/latency across traces, use spans**: `SUM(metrics.tokens)`, `metrics.end - metrics.start`.
- **`metrics.estimated_cost` aggregates but never filters.** It is a computed value, not a stored column — the binder rewrites it to `estimated_cost()`, and a function on the field side cannot be pushed into the index. `SUM(metrics.estimated_cost)` / `AVG(...)` in `select` are fine; **any** use in `where` is blocked (`metrics.estimated_cost IS NOT NULL`, `metrics.estimated_cost > 0`, and the explicit `estimated_cost() ...` all fail with `Cannot execute filter over the index`). To restrict to rows that have cost, filter a real column instead — `metrics.prompt_tokens IS NOT NULL` or `span_attributes.type = 'llm'` — or drop the filter and let the aggregate skip nulls.
- Nested fields always need the parent: `metadata.user_id`, `scores.Factuality`, `span_attributes.name`.
- Braintrust organization members are recorded in `span_attributes.created_by_user_id`. Resolve those IDs in bulk with `lookup_users`. API keys and service tokens are recorded in `span_attributes.created_by_api_key_id`; resolve them in bulk with `lookup_api_keys`. These are system span attributes, not metadata. `metadata.user_id` and similarly named metadata fields are application-defined and must not be assumed to identify Braintrust users or keys.
- `is_root = true` restricts to root spans (needed for root-only metadata/latency).
- Aggregate functions: `count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `percentile(expr, p)` (not `PERCENTILE_CONT`/`percentile_cont`).
- **Aggregation only constrains `select` once you use an aggregate.** A plain projection needs no `group_by` — `select: "id, root_span_id, created, error"` returns a table of rows and is the normal shape for browsing. As soon as `select` contains an aggregate, every _other_ column in `select` must also appear in `group_by`:
  - aggregate + a bare column, no `group_by` → `Cannot mix aggregate and non-aggregate expressions without GROUP BY`
  - `group_by` set, but a selected column is missing from it → `Each measure must contain an aggregate function` (the "measure" is that ungrouped column)
  - Fix either by adding the column to `group_by`, or removing it from `select`.
- Bucketing a timestamp: `date_trunc('<unit>', <field>)`, e.g. `date_trunc('hour', created)`. Units include `minute`, `hour`, `day`, `week`, and arbitrary intervals such as `'300 seconds'`. Works on any timestamp field.
- **This is not ClickHouse, Postgres, or BigQuery SQL.** Builtins from those dialects do not exist and fail with `Unknown function: X` — there is no `date_bin`, `toStartOfHour`/`toStartOfDay`, `toDate`, `countIf`, `has`, or `position*`. Use only the functions listed here; if you need something else, compute it from the returned rows instead of inventing a builtin.
- Time: `now()`, `interval N day` — number **unquoted**, unit **singular** (`interval 7 day`, `interval 24 hour`; plural `7 days`/`24 hours` fails with `interval unit Days`), no quotes (`interval '1 day'` also fails).

## Shape selection

Default to **spans**, and do all grouping / aggregation / sorting there. The tool's strict lint blocks every GROUP BY, aggregate, and ORDER BY on `summary` (`Group by over summary queries is inefficient; consider using a 'traces' or 'spans' shaped query`).

- **Counts, breakdowns, rollups across traces → spans.** Trace count = `COUNT(DISTINCT root_span_id)`; per-trace token/cost totals = `SUM(metrics.tokens)` / `SUM(metrics.estimated_cost)` (add `GROUP BY root_span_id` for per-trace); use `WHERE is_root = true` for one-row-per-trace metadata.
- **summary** is usable **only** as a plain scoped read — a `created` range or an `id`/`root_span_id`, small `LIMIT`, and **no GROUP BY / aggregate / ORDER BY** — to fetch pre-rolled per-trace fields (`metrics.total_tokens`, `metrics.duration`, `span_type_info.*`, averaged scores, root-span input/output).
- **traces** returns all spans of matching traces; keep `select` narrow (large fields are blocked on traces).

## Filters

**A `project_logs` query must be scoped**, or it is rejected with `No filters available for segment elimination`. Either form satisfies this:

- a range filter on `created` (or `_xact_id` / `_pagination_key`) — the usual choice when browsing or aggregating, or
- a filter pinning a specific `id` or `root_span_id` — the right choice when the user names a particular trace or span.

**Do not add a time range to an ID-scoped lookup.** Scoping by `id`/`root_span_id` is sufficient on its own, and bolting on a range silently returns zero rows whenever the target is older than that range — a wrong answer with no error. Only when the query is _not_ ID-scoped and the user gave no time window should you default to `created > now() - interval 1 day`, and say so in `explanation`.

`experiment`, `dataset`, and `view` do **not** require any scope, and adding a `created` range to them can silently exclude rows.

Filters compare a **field to a literal**. Two shapes cannot be pushed into the index and are blocked with `Cannot execute filter over the index`:

- **Comparing two fields to each other.** `span_id = root_span_id` fails — use `is_root = true`. `metrics.end > metrics.start` fails — compare against a literal instead: `(metrics.end - metrics.start) > 1`.
- **A function on the field side.** `lower(span_attributes.name) = 'x'` fails — filter the raw field. This is also why `metrics.estimated_cost` can never be filtered (see above).

Nearly everything else pushes down: `=`, `!=`, `IN`, `IS NULL`/`IS NOT NULL`, numeric comparisons on `metrics.*`, `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`, and `LIKE`/`ILIKE` (leading wildcards included).

For arrays of objects, a dot path matches any element: `classifications."Classifier name".id = 'inconsistent'`. A positional lookup such as `classifications."Classifier name"[0].id` selects only the first element and cannot be pushed into the index. Omit the numeric index when you intend to match any element; keep it only when the position matters.

Full-text search uses the **infix** operator `<field> MATCH '<term>'` (negate with `<field> NOT MATCH '<term>'`) — it is an operator, not a function, so `MATCH(field, 'term')` is a parse error. It matches whole terms lexically, not substrings or meanings: `output MATCH 'time'` does not match `timeout`, and there is no semantic/embedding search. For substring matching use `LIKE`/`ILIKE`.

`input`/`output` sub-paths are a special case — **filterable, but not with ranges**:

- Works: equality (`output.<field> = '<value>'`), null checks (`input.<field> IS NOT NULL`, `output IS NOT NULL`), and negated equality (`NOT (output.<field> = '<value>')`)
- Blocked: numeric range comparisons on these paths — `output.<numeric_field> >= 0.8`, `< 1`, `>`, `BETWEEN` and friends all fail even though the same comparison works fine on `metrics.*`. Compare for equality instead, or project the field and compare the returned rows yourself.
- Grouping by these paths is never allowed — see Grouping.

## Grouping: `group_by` keys must be columnar

This is the single most common lint failure. A `group_by` key has to be a columnar ("fast") field; otherwise the engine cannot push the grouping into the index and blocks with `Cannot push down group by to the index which will result in an inefficient query plan. Reasons: group by or unpivot fields are not Tantivy fast fields: X`.

- **Group-able:** `span_attributes.*` (`name`, `type`, `purpose`, …), `metadata.*` at any depth (`metadata.model`, `metadata.user_id`), `scores.*`, `tags`, `metrics.*`, `error`, `root_span_id`, `span_id`, `is_root`.
- **NOT group-able: `input`, `output`, and any path under them** — `input.<field>`, `output.<field>`, and deeper paths such as `output.<a>.<b>.<c>` all fail, however narrow the sub-path looks. These live inside large document fields rather than columns. Array indexing (`tags[0]`) fails for the same reason.
- **To break down by a non-columnar field, do one of these two things** (both work; pick by whether you already know the values):
  1. **Values known/enumerable** — one aggregate query per value, using an equality filter, which does push down: `select: "COUNT(1) as n"`, `where: "<range> AND <field> = '<value>'"`. Repeat per value and assemble the breakdown yourself.
  2. **Values unknown** — project the field and bucket the rows client-side: `select: "root_span_id, <field>"` with a bounded `limit`, then count the values in the returned rows. Sub-paths like `output.foo` are ordinary projections and are **not** subject to the ≤100 large-field limit (that applies to bare `input`/`output`/`expected`/`metadata`), so a few hundred rows is fine.
     Do not attempt the `group_by` anyway — it is rejected, not merely slow.

The same error also fires for reasons unrelated to the key — they are listed after `Reasons:`, so read them before rewriting:

| Reason text                                                                                                     | Fix                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `group by or unpivot fields are not Tantivy fast fields: X`                                                     | X is not columnar — pick a different key per the lists above                                                                                                        |
| `summary-shaped queries do not support group by pushdown`                                                       | drop `shape: "summary"` and group on `spans` (see Shape selection)                                                                                                  |
| `a filter could not be fully pushed down to Tantivy` / `trace filter could not be fully pushed down to Tantivy` | the group keys are fine — the `where` clause is the problem. Check for `metrics.estimated_cost` first, then field-to-field compares and functions on the field side |
| `subquery filters could not be fully pushed down to Tantivy`                                                    | simplify or remove the sub-filter                                                                                                                                   |
| `sampling with group by pushdown is not supported`                                                              | drop the sample                                                                                                                                                     |

## Recipes (concrete param fills)

**Recent rows**
`select: "id, root_span_id, created, error"`, `order_by: "created DESC"`, `limit: 20`

**Errors in the last day**
`select: "id, root_span_id, created, error"`, `where: "error IS NOT NULL AND created > now() - interval 1 day"`, `limit: 20`

**Count/aggregate per trace (breakdown by model)**
`select: "metadata.model, COUNT(1) as calls, COUNT(DISTINCT root_span_id) as traces"`, `where: "created > now() - interval 1 day"`, `group_by: "metadata.model"`, `order_by: "calls DESC"`, `limit: 20` (shape stays default `spans`)

**Per-trace token / cost totals (on spans, not summary)**
`select: "root_span_id, SUM(metrics.tokens) as tokens, SUM(metrics.estimated_cost) as cost"`, `where: "created > now() - interval 1 day"`, `group_by: "root_span_id"`, `order_by: "tokens DESC"`, `limit: 20`

**Breakdown by tool call**
`select: "span_attributes.name, COUNT(1) as calls"`, `where: "created > now() - interval 1 day AND span_attributes.type = 'tool'"`, `group_by: "span_attributes.name"`, `order_by: "calls DESC"`, `limit: 20`

**Latency percentile (root spans only)**
`select: "PERCENTILE(metrics.end - metrics.start, 0.95) as p95"`, `where: "created > now() - interval 1 day AND is_root = true"`, `limit: 1`

**Full trace context for errors**
`select: "id, root_span_id, created, error"`, `where: "error IS NOT NULL AND created > now() - interval 1 day"`, `shape: "traces"`, `limit: 20` — keep the `select` narrow; large fields (`input`/`output`) on `traces` shape are separately blocked (see table).

## Error substring → cause → fix

| Error contains                                                            | Cause                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Fix                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Field 'X' not found in schema`                                           | bare/wrong field name in `select`/`where`/`group_by`/`order_by`                                                                                                                                                                                       | qualify it: `span_attributes.type`, `span_parents`, `metadata.X`, `scores.X`                                                                                                              |
| `Unsupported expression: invalid interval value`                          | quoted interval, e.g. `interval '1 day'`                                                                                                                                                                                                              | unquote: `interval 1 day`                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Unknown function: X`                                                     | wrong builtin name (`PERCENTILE_CONT`, `MATCH_AGAINST`, etc.)                                                                                                                                                                                         | use the real name, e.g. `percentile(expr, p)`                                                                                                                                             |
| `Group by over summary queries is inefficient`                            | any GROUP BY / aggregate / ORDER BY on `shape: "summary"`                                                                                                                                                                                             | move to `shape: "spans"` (default): `COUNT(DISTINCT root_span_id)`, `SUM(metrics.tokens)`, etc. — summary is read-only for pre-rolled fields                                              |
| `No filters available for segment elimination`                            | no selective filter on `created`/`_xact_id`/`_pagination_key`, or no `id`/`root_span_id` scope                                                                                                                                                        | add a time range to `where`, e.g. `created > now() - interval 1 day`                                                                                                                      |
| `Cannot push down group by to the index`                                  | a `group_by` key is not columnar (`input`/`output` or a path under them, array index), or the reason names a filter/shape/sample issue                                                                                                                | see Grouping — pick a columnar key, or fix the reason listed after `Reasons:`                                                                                                             |
| `group by on a dynamic expression ... not columnar-compatible`            | `group_by` uses a function/expression (`lower(metadata.model)`)                                                                                                                                                                                       | group by the raw field; post-process casing/derivation after the query returns                                                                                                            |
| `standalone Project above Index search ... sort pushdown may have failed` | `order_by` on a non-indexed column (`metrics.*`, computed expr, `root_span_id`, or multi-key)                                                                                                                                                         | sort by `created` only, or drop `order_by` and sort client-side; if already scoped by `id`/`root_span_id`, `force_ignore_linter: true`                                                    |
| `projects large fields (...) without LIMIT <= 100`                        | `select` includes `input`/`output`/similar with `limit` > 100 on spans/summary                                                                                                                                                                        | set `limit` ≤ 100, or scope `where` to a specific `id`/`root_span_id`                                                                                                                     |
| `projects large fields (...) on traces shape`                             | `select` includes large fields with `shape: "traces"`                                                                                                                                                                                                 | switch to `spans`/`summary`, or scope `where` to specific ids                                                                                                                             |
| `Cannot mix aggregate and non-aggregate expressions without GROUP BY`     | `select` has an aggregate plus a bare column, and `group_by` is empty                                                                                                                                                                                 | add the bare column to `group_by`, or drop it from `select`                                                                                                                               |
| `Each measure must contain an aggregate function`                         | `group_by` is set but a column in `select` is not in it                                                                                                                                                                                               | add that column to `group_by`, or drop it from `select`                                                                                                                                   |
| `Cannot execute filter over the index`                                    | `where` filter isn't pushdown-friendly. Most common cause by far: `metrics.estimated_cost` in `where` (becomes `ESTIMATED_COST()`). Also: comparing two fields (`metrics.end > metrics.start`), or a function on the field side (`lower(name) = 'x'`) | drop the cost filter (aggregate it in `select` instead) or filter `metrics.prompt_tokens`; compare a field to a literal, not to another field; filter the raw field, not a function of it |
| `Limit must be <= 1000`                                                   | `limit` over 1000                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | cap `limit` at 1000; page with `where` scoping instead of raising it further                                                                                                              |
